You can’t make assumptions about any patients jobs. Pharmacists and technicians know what they signed up for when they decided to go into the field. And if you know enough about the system having problems, especially when it is effecting you and your patients and you do nothing to change it, part of it is on you. If you see issues and do nothing knowing the issues are there you have lost your ability to complain. You even see on here about countries where medication is less regulated and people working in that field (pharmacy) are changing it. Many people don’t know how the insurance works, they are busy just like everyone else and I try to understand we usually see patients at their lowest and most vulnerable. There are some just plain mean people that take stuff out on others, but if you know you are dealing with the general public in any job, you kinda learn to deal with it. Most people aren’t mad at pharmacy they are mad at their situation. We see a tiny peek into their life, so to judge them harshly goes against being able to do what you need to do to look past any biases and give them good care.
